A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe the same AMI-ME study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation results, LLM benchmarks, segmentation and end-to-end experiments, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 5 and 7 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The objective classification, topic segmentation, LLM scoring, and temporal alignment procedures remain identical, including the prompts in Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both use the same 130 AMI meetings and 2,459 segments, covering business scenarios, film selection, office relocation, and evaluation from raw speech.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including the LLM benchmarks, Absence/BERTSeg/SumSeg segmentation comparisons, and Qwen3/Gemini comparison in Appendix B.2.

E3.justification: Section 7 and Appendices D–E retain identical metrics, model configurations, input conditions, preprocessing, and ablation settings.

E4.justification: The context/objective ablations, duration analysis, inter-LLM consistency analysis, and segmentation-error analysis in Appendices E–H are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including annotator ICC estimates, sampling information, and p < 0.05 significance markers in Tables 1–3.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains Qwen3-32B (non-reasoning)'s all-meetings Spearman correlation of 0.6445; appendix results also remain identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, alignment equation, duration-weighted derivation in Appendix A, and segmentation-bound reasoning in Appendix H are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about temporal evaluation, AMI-ME, the automatic framework, and benchmark contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of segmentation penalties, transcription robustness, and context effects are unchanged, as are limitations concerning participant well-being, rating linearity, and real-world applicability.

D1.justification: Annotation instructions, prompts, hardware and vLLM disclosures, and the dataset/code access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work, citations, references, and research positioning remain identical, including the claimed first application of LLM-as-a-judge to meeting effectiveness.

P1.justification: The author email line is expanded, changing Chu's address from chu@nlp.ist.i.kyoto-u.ac.jp to chu@i.kyoto-u.ac.jp. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; body wording and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–4 retain identical content, captions, and placement. Pages 2–18 render identically; first-page differences are confined to contact/version text.

improvement.justification: Only author contact information and the arXiv stamp change. Scientific content, empirical evidence, technical documentation, and presentation of results remain identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
